title: Phase 1 evaluation of APN401, an autologous CBL-B-silenced PBMC therapy, in advanced solid tumors

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Phase 1 evaluation of APN401, an autologous CBL-B-silenced PBMC therapy, in advanced solid tumors》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0010】Immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment, with immune checkpoint inhibitors producing durable clinical benefit across multiple tumor types. However, many patients with advanced malignancies fail to achieve sustained responses due to immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments, antigen heterogeneity, and progressive dysfunction of tumor-reactive T cells.1,2,3,4,5 Additional immunotherapeutic approaches, including cellular therapies, have demonstrated activity in selected settings but remain limited in solid tumors by impaired tumor infiltration, antigen escape, and manufacturing complexity.6,7,8 These challenges highlight the need for complementary strategies that enhance intrinsic immune cell function.

【Introduction · p0015】Intracellular signaling pathways regulating activation thresholds represent an emerging target space for immune modulation. Casitas B-lineage lymphoma proto-oncogene B (CBL-B), an E3 ubiquitin ligase, is a key negative regulator of antigen receptor signaling that increases the threshold for T cell activation.9,10 Preclinical studies have shown that CBL-B inhibition enhances T cell activation and promotes antitumor immunity.11,12 Furthermore, CBL-B regulates both adaptive and innate immune-cell function, including T and natural killer (NK) cells, providing a rationale for therapeutic CBL-B inhibition across multiple immune-cell compartments.9,13

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Phase 1 evaluation of APN401, an autologous CBL-B-silenced PBMC therapy, in advanced solid tumors》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Patients and treatments · p0035】Nineteen patients were screened across APN401-103 and APN401-104, and 17 patients received at least one APN401 infusion and comprised the pooled safety population (Table 1; Tables S1 and S2). Patients represented a heterogeneous population of advanced treatment-refractory solid tumors and had received at least two prior lines of systemic therapy. In APN401-104, patients received a median of 4 prior lines of therapy (range, 3–8), and 6 patients had prior exposure to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Patients received escalating doses ranging from 5 × 106 to 4.5 × 107 PBMCs/kg and completed a median of 3 treatment cycles (range, 1–6). Dose escalation in APN401-103 evaluated dose levels 1 (5 × 106 PBMCs/kg) and 2 (1.5 × 107 PBMCs/kg), whereas APN401-104 evaluated dose levels 2 and 3 followed by expansion at dose level 3 (4.5 × 107 PBMCs/kg), which was subsequently selected as the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). Treatment discontinuation primarily reflected disease progression or clinical deterioration in this heavily pretreated population. Additional reasons included withdrawal in the patient’s best interest (n = 4), patient withdrawal (n = 1) of consent, and out-of-specification (OOS, n = 2) manufacturing batches identified before infusion (Table S2). Overall, 51 of 56 manufactured batches met pre-infusion release specifications (Figure S1). APN401 was manufactured and administered as a fresh, non-cryopreserved cell product without an intervening cryopreservation and thawing step. Of the five OOS batches, two did not meet the predefined identity specification and three did not meet the predefined quantity specification. These events did not result in modification of the APN401 manufacturing process but informed subsequent narrowing of the acceptance specification for the leukapheresis starting material. Post-electroporation DP viability was 76.4% ± 7.2% of viable PBMCs, and functional characterization demonstrated reduction of CBLB mRNA by 56.0% ± 14.2% and reduction of CBL-B protein expression by 91.4% ± 10.7% relative to matched controls.

【Representative patients with immune correlates · p0075】Two patients with extended longitudinal immune monitoring are shown to illustrate heterogeneous immune response kinetics observed during APN401 treatment.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Phase 1 evaluation of APN401, an autologous CBL-B-silenced PBMC therapy, in advanced solid tumors》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Introduction · p0025】Here, we report results from two phase 1 studies evaluating APN401 in a broad population of patients with advanced treatment-refractory solid tumors, reflecting the safety and feasibility objectives of early-phase development rather than patient selection based on established tumor-specific sensitivity to CBL-B inhibition in immune cells. Hence, the studies focused on safety, manufacturing feasibility, and exploratory immune activity associated with transient intracellular checkpoint modulation.

【Treatment-associated immune activation · p0065】Comparison of baseline and post-cycle 1 samples demonstrated early modulation of multiple immune parameters (Figure 4A), including changes in circulating CD8+ T cell populations, memory-associated T cell subsets, activation-associated markers, and soluble immune mediators. Post-cycle 2 analyses demonstrated continued immune remodeling across lymphoid and myeloid compartments (Figures 4B and 4C), including changes in CD8+ T cell abundance, CD8+/CD4+ T cell ratios, B cell populations, monocyte subsets, and myeloid-derived suppressor cell (MDSC)-associated parameters. Longitudinal analyses also demonstrated delayed upregulation of inhibitory receptors including PD-1, TIM-3, and LAG-3 during treatment (Figure S2). Patients with SD demonstrated longitudinal changes in markers associated with cytotoxic T cell activation and systemic immune remodeling, including increased CD137+ and TIM-3+ CD8+ T cells, elevated plasma interferon-γ (IFN-γ), and expansion of circulating B cell populations. In contrast, PD was associated with higher monocyte levels and increased plasma IL-10. These immune changes coincided with expansion of dominant TCRβ clonotypes in selected patients (Figure S3). The antigen specificity of these expanded clonotypes was not determined.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Phase 1 evaluation of APN401, an autologous CBL-B-silenced PBMC therapy, in advanced solid tumors》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1 · fig1】Figure 1 APN401 manufacturing workflow and proposed mechanism of action(A) APN401 is manufactured from autologous peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) collected by leukapheresis. Following closed-system PBMC purification, unfractionated PBMCs are electroporated with CBL-B-targeting siRNA, followed by removal of cell debris and residual reagents and final formulation of APN401. The drug-product (DP) undergoes pre-infusion release testing for appearance, identity, quantity (cell count), purity, viability, and endotoxin before reinfusion, with a vein-to-vein time of <24 h. Sterility and functional characterization of retained DP samples is performed post-infusion and includes assessment of CBLB mRNA knockdown and CBL-B protein downregulation and IL-2 induction following T cell receptor (TCR) stimulation. (B) Proposed mechanism of action of APN401. Following reinfusion, antigen encounter, and TCR activation are expected to induce CBL-B expression as part of physiological negative-feedback signaling. CBL-B-specific siRNA introduced during APN401 manufacturing limits activation-induced CBL-B expression, thereby transiently reducing negative regulation of TCR signaling and enhancing T cell activation, cytokine production, proliferation, and cytotoxic function, which may improve recognition and killing of tumor cells.APC, antigen-presenting cell; CBL-B, Casitas B-lineage lymphoma proto-oncogene B; siRNA, small interfering RNA; TCR, T cell receptor. Created in BioRender. Kuttke, M. (2026) https://BioRender.com/qzshtzm.

【Figure 2 · fig2】Figure 2 Tumor response and treatment exposure following APN401 therapy(A) Longitudinal percentage change in target-lesion size from baseline in patients with available target-lesion measurements (n = 10). Dashed lines indicate RECIST v.1.1 thresholds for partial response (−30%) and progressive disease (+20%). (B) Swimmer plot showing treatment exposure and clinical course in the safety population (n = 17). Each bar represents an individual patient and indicates the duration of APN401 treatment. Symbols indicate stable disease (α), progressive disease (β), or early termination (γ). ∗Reduction in target lesion measurements observed during follow-up. (C) Maximum percentage change in target-lesion size from baseline in patients with available target-lesion measurements (n = 10). Each bar represents an individual patient; colors indicate stable disease or progressive disease according to RECIST v.1.1.BOR, best overall response; RECIST, Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors.

【Figure 3 · fig3】Figure 3 Clinical and radiographic assessments in selected APN401-treated patientsClinical status and radiographic tumor assessments were evaluated longitudinally in selected patients with sufficient follow-up to assess longitudinal tumor kinetics. ECOG performance status and target lesion measurements were collected at screening, during treatment cycles, and during follow-up assessments. Stacked plots show the sum of target lesion (T) measurements over time. Non-target lesions (NT) and new lesions are indicated where applicable. Tumor assessments were performed according to RECIST v.1.1 criteria. Patient 104-05-003 did not receive cycle 4 because no DP was manufactured.
